summary: The owner confirmed the 550 locations and requested retail-like randomness on 2026-09-12. Ordinary pads roll independently at 30%; Pleasant Valley and Ranchito police stations clamp their four pad rolls to one or two cars. This is tunable server population policy, not a measured retail percentage. Explicit zero/one chances select none/all; null retains legacy count/spacing.

rows.source: Owner follow-up 2026-09-12: keep correct locations but randomize occupancy; police department should have one car, sometimes two
rows.note: 30% is chosen server tuning, not a recovered retail probability. Ordinary pads remain independent. For fractional chances, each identified police station clamps its four seeded rolls to one or two cars (second car probability 34.83% at the default). All 550 confirmed locations, families and poses remain eligible and unchanged. Configurable as vehicles.spawnChance or CRANBERRY_VEHICLE_SPAWN_CHANCE (0-1); explicit 0 disables vehicles and 1 fills every pad. See docs/vehicle-randomness-20260912.md.

rows.source: C:\Z1\Server\Zone\ZoneCombat.cs:189 and ZoneVehicleResources.cs:119 - the owner's own round-25 regression fix: within the window one impact costs its PEAK, once, not once per packet
rows.note: Not tuning, a correctness requirement. The 47 live 8e 01 records recovered from C:\Aug2017\logs are two interleaved RAMPS (7, 14, 22, 30, 38, 46 ... and 262, 272, 283, 293, 303 ...), i.e. the client re-reports one continuing event with a running total. rows.source: src/Cranberry.Zone/Vehicles/VehicleDamage.cs - Cranberry design; Vehicles.txt EXPLODE_DAMAGE and EXPLODE_RANGE are 0 on every row and DestroyedInfo.txt's TRIGGERED_ABILITY 1111205 is TargetPhysicsAreaAroundSelf, a physics impulse (RADIUS_MAX 8, params 3000/8000/4/8), not a damage field
rows.note: UNRULED, and ZERO on purpose. The explosion damage is not in this build and the owner's Z1 has no destroy-on-zero rule either (ZoneVehicleResources.cs:316-349 floors the condition at 1 and says so). Occupants are put out of the wreck; nothing invents what that costs them. CRANBERRY_VEHICLE_WRECK_DAMAGE is here for the owner to rule on.

rows.source: src/Cranberry.Zone/Vehicles/VehicleBoost.cs - Cranberry design; the client's own AbilityEx VehicleTurbo rows carry RESOURCE_FIRST_COST, RESOURCE_COST_PER_MSEC, FLAG_PAY_RESOURCE_COST and EXPIRE_MSEC all 0
rows.note: UNRULED. Only the MAGNITUDE of a boost is the client's (MoveInfo mode 2: OffRoader 90, Pickup 80, Police 105, ATV 100 against a normal 85); the COST is the server's. Four times the cruising rate puts a full tank at about five minutes of continuous boost against twenty-one minutes of cruising. The owner's Z1 carries the same figure but its own comment sources it to the forbidden tree (ZoneVehicleResources.cs:89), so it is NOT adopted - this is Cranberry's number, chosen independently.

rows.source: the August binary: 0f 33 Character.Turbo parser FUN_140a65200, handler FUN_140af9ca0 case 0x33 - value 0 SETS bit 0 of actor+0x4f8, any other value clears it, and the field is pre-seeded to 2
rows.note: UNRULED as a POLARITY. The byte itself is the client's; which of its two states means boost-granted is inferred - 0 sets reads more like turbo-BLOCKED-cleared than turbo-on. One live press settles it, and CRANBERRY_VEHICLE_TURBO_BYTE flips it in one word.
